posts.content:
Update on the 9.8 CVSS TCP/IP RCE in the Linux kernel (CVE-2026-98432): we've detected what appears to be a threat actor activity scanning the entire internet for exposed affected systems. Our own scanning also suggests that the number of potential targets is high, therefore there is an increased likelihood of threat actors attempting to develop exploits for the vulnerability.

while CVE-2026-98432 is believed to require MPTCP to be enabled in the kernel, as well as a listening app/service which binds an MPTCP socket, which many have suggested should be rare, several kernels including Debian enable MPTCP by default.

Additionally, Go 1.24+ binds MPTCP sockets by default if the option is enabled in the kernel, so anything built on top of Go (including Caddy) will create the required MPTCP listener.

The mitigation of setting net.mptcp.enabled=0 disabled MPTCP, but does not apply to existing sockets, so any applications that have bound MPTCP sockets need to be restarted, otherwise the system remains exploitable.

You can check if your server is running any MPTCP listeners with the following command: sudo ss -Mlnp

On 2026-10-30 our preliminary internet-wide scan of port 443 confirmed that there are approximately 2,102,043 servers that are successfully reachable via an MPTCP connection. A deeper scan which attempts to connect to each endpoint on port 443 and negotiate a full TLS connection with MPTCP enabled returned about 762,774 systems.

Neither scan can confirm that these are unpatched kernels, just total exposure, but it's a lot more systems than expected. Since a valid HTTP connection is not required to exploit the vulnerability, the total attack surface is likely closer to the 2.1 million number than the 763k one.

As of today (2026-11-02), we've picked up several residential proxies and VPNs scanning the internet on port 443 using MPTCP-enabled connections. Since regular scanners do not negotiate MPTCP by default, and no data is being sent to the HTTP server over 443, we strongly suspect this activity is scanning for CVE-2026-98432 specifically. The use of residential proxies and RU-based VPN servers suggests that this is likely threat actor scanning, rather than security researchers.

Currently there are no known publicly available remote code execution exploits, but there are several denial of service proof-of-concepts floating around. This code gives threat actors a starting point to begin attempting to weaponize the vulnerability. Building exploits for the vulnerability is reported to be extremely difficult, but several state-sponsored threat actors likely have the resources required to succeed.

🚨 Critical Linux kernel flaw could allow remote root code execution; CVE-2026-98432

A use-after-free vulnerability in the Linux IPv4 TCP handshake path allows an unauthenticated attacker to trigger memory corruption by sending specially timed packets to a listening service.

Successful exploitation could crash the system or potentially execute arbitrary code as root.
⠀
• CVSS: 9.8
• Affected: Linux kernel 4.4 and later
• Attack vector: Network
• Privileges required: None
• User interaction: None
• Active exploitation: Not reported
⠀
Fixed kernel branches:

• 5.10.272
• 5.15.223
• 6.1.190
• 6.6.159
• 6.12.113
• 6.18.56
• 7.2.10
• 7.3
⠀
Administrators should install their distribution’s updated kernel and reboot to activate the fix.

In case you missed it: CVE-2026-98432 is a critical (CVSS 9.8) bug in the Linux kernel's TCP code. It's been there since 2016, so virtually every Linux server on the planet has it, and it can be hit remotely. Anthropic says it built a working exploit that gets root on a server. A total takeover.

Debian patched it on October 16. Ubuntu still doesn't have a patch more than two weeks later. Every supported release, LTS included, is listed as "Vulnerable".

CVE-2026-98432.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period

tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq->ireq_opt to the
child socket (newinet->inet_opt) without copying it.

Another cpu can concurrently process a retransmitted SYN for the same
request socket, and send a SYNACK from tcp_check_req().
tcp_v4_send_synack() and inet_csk_route_req() read ireq->ireq_opt
under rcu_read_lock() only, and ip_build_and_send_pkt() and
ip_options_build() then read opt->optlen twice.

Note that the SYNACK timer itself is not an issue: it holds a
reference on its request socket, and inet_csk_reqsk_queue_drop()
calls timer_delete_sync() before the child can be freed.

Since commit 079096f103fa ("tcp/dccp: install syn_recv requests
into ehash table"), request sockets are processed without holding
the listener lock, so nothing prevents the child socket from being
freed while the SYNACK is still being built. TCP child sockets do
not have SOCK_RCU_FREE, and inet_sock_destruct() frees inet_opt
with a plain kfree(), leading to a use-after-free in
ip_options_build().

A similar issue exists with request socket migration
(net.ipv4.tcp_migrate_req=1, or a BPF_SK_REUSEPORT_SELECT_OR_MIGRATE
program). reqsk_timer_handler() clones the request socket with
inet_reqsk_clone(), so that the old request socket and its clone
share the same ireq_opt, then reqsk_migrate_reset() clears the
pointer in the old one. Another cpu holding a reference on the old
request socket can still be using these options (sending a SYNACK,
or creating a child in tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock()) when the clone is
freed, and tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() also uses a plain kfree().

Readers already use RCU, and other paths replacing inet_opt
(do_ip_setsockopt(), cipso_v4_sock_setattr()...) already use
kfree_rcu(). Use kfree_rcu() in inet_sock_destruct() and
tcp_v4_reqsk_destructor() as well.

IPv6 is not affected by the first issue, because tcp_v6_syn_recv_sock()
duplicates the options. tcp_v6_reqsk_destructor() has the same
migration issue with ipv6_opt, which is only set by CALIPSO. This
will be addressed in a separate patch.

CVE-2026-81572.description:
In CodeMeter Runtime from version 8.40 to (excluding) 8.41a and 9.00 to (excluding) 9.10, cmu.exe --create-io --file C: creates a predictable temporary file under C:\CM-Stick. The directory and
file paths are not properly checked for NTFS reparse points, such as junctions or symbolic links, before file
operations are performed. A local attacker can create a junction at the temporary file that points to an arbitrary
system path. Because CodeMeter Runtime runs with System privileges, this could allow arbitrary files to be deleted
with System privileges and potentially enable local privilege escalation.

takeover.

posts.content: CVE-2026-4327 CVSS 8.8: RCE in The Welcomizer WordPress plugin up to 2.8.1. Missing auth checks plus eval() on user input let unauthenticated attackers run code. No patch confirmed. Audit or remove the plugin now. #CVE #infosec #WordPress https://www.valtersit.com/cve/CVE-2026-4327/

CVE-2026-4327.description: The The Welcomizer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to and including 2.8.1. This is due to missing authorization checks on the twiz_ajax_callback AJAX action's 'savesection' handler combined with the use of eval() to execute user-supplied 'custom logic' code on the frontend. The AJAX handler at twiz-ajax.php verifies a nonce but performs no current_user_can() capability check for the ACTION_SAVE_SECTION case. Furthermore, the nonce is exposed to any authenticated user through the directly-accessible twiz-ajax.js.php file which loads WordPress and outputs the nonce. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary PHP code via the twiz_custom_logic POST parameter when saving a section with output choice 'twiz_logic_output'.

CVE-2024-56337.description:
Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition vulnerability in Apache Tomcat.

This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.1, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.33, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.97.
The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are 
known to be affected: 8.5.0 though 8.5.100. Other, older, EOL versions 
may also be affected.


The mitigation for CVE-2024-50379 was incomplete.

Users running Tomcat on a case insensitive file system with the default servlet write enabled (readonly initialisation 
parameter set to the non-default value of false) may need additional configuration to fully mitigate CVE-2024-50379 depending on which version of Java they are using with Tomcat:
- running on Java 8 or Java 11: the system property sun.io.useCanonCaches must be explicitly set to false (it defaults to true)
- running on Java 17: the system property sun.io.useCanonCaches, if set, must be set to false (it defaults to false)
- running on Java 21 onwards: no further configuration is required (the system property and the problematic cache have been removed)

Tomcat 11.0.3, 10.1.35 and 9.0.99 onwards will include checks that sun.io.useCanonCaches is set appropriately before allowing the default servlet to be write enabled on a case insensitive file system. Tomcat will also set sun.io.useCanonCaches to false by default where it can.

posts.content:
🚨 Critical zero-click Android RCE patched; CVE-2026-58868

A heap buffer overflow in Android’s Framework component could allow remote code execution without additional privileges or user interaction.

The flaw resides in the onOutputReceived function within FrameDecoder.cpp, where an out-of-bounds write can occur while processing media frames.

• Severity: Critical
• CVSS: Not yet assigned
• Affected: Android 14, 15, 16, 16 QPR2 and 17
• Fixed: Security patch level 2026-11-01 or later
• PoC: No public exploit identified
• Exploitation: No confirmed in-the-wild attacks

Administrators should aim for the 2026-11-05 patch level or later, which includes this fix and the remaining November security updates for kernel and hardware components.

Source: https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/2026/2026-11-01

posts.content: CVE-2026-99247 | HIGH severity in Linux kernel 5.19: Kernel may crash (NULL pointer dereference) during early boot if tracing is disabled & trace buffer allocation fails. Patch available — apply ASAP to prevent boot failures. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-99247-tracing-do-not-initialize-tracefs-work-if-tracing-is-disabled-in-linux-kernel-11ff73f18055537a #OffSeq #Linux #Kernel #Vuln

CVE-2026-99247.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

tracing: Do not initialize tracefs work if tracing is disabled

If trace buffer allocation fails during early boot (e.g.  in
early_trace_init() -> allocate_trace_buffers()), tracing_disabled is
left set to 1 and the global trace array events list remains
uninitialized.

Later during boot, tracer_init_tracefs() (invoked via fs_initcall)
queues tracerfs_init_work asynchronously without checking if tracing was
disabled.  When tracer_init_tracefs_work_func() runs, it calls
event_trace_init() and init_tracer_tracefs(&global_trace, NULL)
unconditionally.  This leads to __find_event_file() dereferencing an
uninitialized tr->events list, causing an early boot NULL pointer
dereference Oops:

  BUG: Kernel NULL pointer dereference on read at 0x00000010
  Faulting instruction address: 0xc000000000485be0
  Oops: Kernel access of bad area, sig: 7 [#1]
  ...
  NIP [c000000000485be0] __find_event_file+0x70/0x3c0
  LR  [c000000000448874] init_tracer_tracefs+0x274/0xc80
  Call Trace:
   init_tracer_tracefs+0x274/0xc80
   tracer_init_tracefs_work_func+0x50/0x320
   process_one_work+0x1e8/0x5c0
   worker_thread+0x1dc/0x3d0
   kthread+0x194/0x1b0
   start_kernel_thread+0x14/0x18

Check tracing_disabled at the beginning of tracer_init_tracefs_work_func()
and return immediately if tracing is disabled or failed to initialize,
preventing the crash.

posts.content:
@dansup Tried adding the .env variable but it didn't seem to have any effect.

I tried looking through the code, I think this was the commit that blocked the private IPs:
https://github.com/pixelfed/pixelfed/commit/0e0de62dd9767f8da8a76fa0ff4e5e2be5981744

Am assuming it's related to the SSRF mentioned in CVE-2026-71246.

It looks like there is a boolean env variable for "AP_SKIP_LOCAL_URL_CHECKS". Not sure if that will do something.

CVE-2026-71246.description: Pixelfed's SearchController (behind the auth middleware) accepts a URL via its remote-search parameters and fetches it server-side through ActivityPubFetchService, whose validateUrl() only blocks the literal hosts 127.0.0.1, localhost, and ::1 and requires https, without checking the resolved IP against private, internal, or link-local ranges (e.g. 169.254.169.254). Optional DNS validation is disabled by default and, when enabled, only confirms a DNS record exists without filtering by IP range. The fetch response body is returned to the requester only when the Content-Type matches an ActivityPub content type, making this a semi-blind but authenticated SSRF primitive reachable by any logged-in user.

posts.content:
Veeam Patches Critical Remote Code Execution Flaws in Management Pack for MS System Center

Veeam has patched three vulnerabilities in its Management Pack for Microsoft System Center, including a critical unauthenticated remote code execution flaw (CVE-2023-22793). These bugs allow attackers to take control of monitoring servers and potentially move laterally through virtualization environments.

**If you use Veeam Management Pack for Microsoft System Center version 9.x, upgrade to version 13.1.0.334 ASAP. These flaws let attackers take full control of your monitoring server. If you're on a build older than 9a (9.1.0.3107), update to 9a first, then upgrade to 13.1.0.334, since Veeam won't release a separate fix for 9.x.**
#cybersecurity #infosec #advisory #vulnerability
https://beyondmachines.net/event_details/veeam-patches-critical-remote-code-execution-flaws-in-management-pack-for-ms-system-center-7-n-b-d-i/gD2P6Ple2L

posts.content: CVE-2026-120534 | CRITICAL vuln (CVSS 9.8) in ACF Extended PRO ≤0.9.2.6 allows unauthenticated code injection via render_field. Prevent by disabling 'shortcode_preview' & ensuring OpenSSL is present. Patch status pending. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-120534-cwe-434-unrestricted-upload-of-file-with-dangerous-type-in-acf-extended-advanced-24aed413b4a5b6e4 #OffSeq #WordPress #Vuln

CVE-2026-120534.description: The Advanced Custom Fields: Extended PRO plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Limited Code Injection in all versions up to, and including, 0.9.2.6 via the render_field function. This is due to insufficient validation of form configuration parameters before merging into field settings and passing to call_user_func_array in the render_field method. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to call arbitrary WordPress functions with controlled arguments. Method 1 requires the administrator to enable the non-default 'shortcode_preview' setting for the target form, while Method 2 requires the server environment to lack OpenSSL functions, causing ACF Pro's acf_decrypt to fall back to unverified base64 decoding.

Linux kernel vulnerabilities this week: 129 CVEs, including critical iSCSI flaws CVE-2026-99154 and CVE-2026-99153. Get the kernel security update.

#LinuxKernel #Linux #CVE202699154 #CVE202699153 #iSCSI #KernelSecurity #PatchNow #Vulnerability

https://securityonline.info/linux-kernel-vulnerabilities-oct-26-nov-1-2026/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-99153.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libiscsi: Validate the ITT reflected in a Reject PDU

A Reject PDU carries a copy of the header it rejects, and
iscsi_handle_reject() takes the ITT out of that copy to find the task to
clean up:

      memcpy(&rejected_pdu, data, sizeof(struct iscsi_hdr));
      ...
      task = iscsi_itt_to_task(conn, rejected_pdu.itt);

That value is whatever the target put there. iscsi_itt_to_task() bounds
the index against cmds_max and checks nothing else, so any task in the
pool can be named, and iscsi_nop_out_rsp() then completes it.

An index that has never been used gives a NULL task->conn: the pool is
zeroed at session setup and conn is assigned only when a task is
allocated. If the task was used and returned, iscsi_complete_task() hits
its WARN_ON_ONCE(task->state == ISCSI_TASK_FREE) and the refcount
underflows. An in-flight SCSI command is completed as successful - a 1
MiB read returned 1048576 with none of its buffer written and no
warning.

Validate the reflected ITT the way iscsi_itt_to_ctask() validates a
command ITT, and require the task to be in flight and not a SCSI
command.

Linux kernel vulnerabilities this week: 129 CVEs, including critical iSCSI flaws CVE-2026-99154 and CVE-2026-99153. Get the kernel security update.

CVE-2026-99154.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

scsi: libiscsi: Reject a negative task index from parse_pdu_itt

A transport that implements parse_pdu_itt hands libiscsi an index taken
from the PDU, and both lookups bound it from above only:

      if (i >= session->cmds_max)

i and cmds_max are both int, so a negative index passes and
session->cmds[i] is read from before the array.

be2iscsi produces one. beiscsi_parse_pdu() assigns the raw tag,

      *index = (int)itt;

and beiscsi_complete_pdu() forwards an unsolicited NOP-In from the
hardware async ring without replacing its ITT, so the value is the
target's. It also reports the session's own age rather than the one in
the tag, which leaves the age comparison in iscsi_verify_itt() with
nothing to reject.

Bound the index from below in both lookups.

We published two more exploit and detection packages to @vulncheck's Initial Access community repo today. Neither CVE has been reported exploited in the wild yet, but both product ecosystems have been exploited in the past. Today's haul:

- CVE-2026-92122: A Groovy sandbox escape in the Jenkins Script Security Plugin, which (per Jenkins) is installed on 98.8% of all Jenkins controllers. FOFA shows ~80K Jenkins servers online.

- CVE-2026-8857: A command injection vulnerability in MediaWiki's EasyTimeline plugin (which was enabled in Fandom). A Nuclei template has been available since August, and there are ~25K MediaWiki instances online (which means that if this thing really hasn't been exploited yet - dubious - it probably will be).

Both #exploits come with Suricata and Snort rules, vulnerable target Docker containers, PCAPs, and ASM queries.
https://github.com/vulncheck-oss/initial-access-community

CVE-2026-8857.description:
A vulnerability in Wikimedia Foundation timeline.

 This vulnerability is associated with program files scripts/EasyTimeline.Pl, includes/Timeline.Php.



This issue affects timeline: from * before 1.46.0, 1.45.4, 1.44.6, 1.43.9.

posts.content:
3 threats SOC teams should know about this week 🛡️

My site Intel60 tracked 119 security stories this week. 34 were rated critical, and CISA added 10 bugs to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities list. These are the three I’d put at the top of a SOC’s list:

1️⃣ Cisco firewall VPN zero-day (CVE-2026-76418)
Attackers are exploiting a flaw in the remote-access VPN of Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD. It’s the second Cisco firewall zero-day since August.
🔎 SOC angle: patch now, then review VPN logs for unusual sessions. Edge devices are where attackers get in first.

2️⃣ Claude Code extension backdoored in Open VSX
The extension in the Open VSX registry was compromised to install a persistent SSH backdoor on developer machines. Cursor’s marketplace was also affected and temporarily shut down.
🔎 SOC angle: check developer endpoints for unexpected SSH keys and new authorized_keys entries. Developer tools are now part of the supply-chain attack surface.

3️⃣ Ivanti Connect Secure flaws added to KEV
CISA flagged a missing-authentication flaw (CVE-2026-111357) that can be chained with other bugs. The federal deadline is Nov 2, which tells you how urgent CISA considers it.
🔎 SOC angle: if you run Ivanti, patch, then hunt for signs of compromise. With Ivanti, patching alone hasn’t always removed attackers who were already in.

The pattern this week: the entry points are edge devices and developer tools. Watch what sits at the perimeter and what your developers install.

I track these with Intel60, a free tool I built that turns security news into 60-word, severity-rated briefs every 30 minutes: https://intel60.app

What was the biggest story on your radar this week? 👇

#cybersecurity #SOC #threatintel #infosec #blueteam #vulnerabilitymanagement

CVE-2026-76418.description: A vulnerability in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to cause the device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) condition. This vulnerability is due to logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted request when connecting to the SSL remote access VPN. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to cause the affected device to reload, resulting in a DoS condition.

CVE-2026-119085 - Template injection in the publishing component of Virtual Engineering Workbench

Bulletin ID: 2026-162-AWS Publication Date: 11/02/2026 09:30 AM PST
Description:
Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) is an open-source platform where platform engineers define and publish development environments, and developers provision them on demand ...

https://aws.amazon.com/security/security-bulletins/rss/2026-162-aws/

#aws #security

CVE-2026-119085.description:
Improper neutralization of special elements used in a template engine in the publishing component of Amazon Virtual Engineering Workbench (VEW) could allow a remote authenticated third party to run arbitrary code with the permissions of the publishing Lambda's IAM role. This could allow access to data and resources across all tenant projects. The code is reachable through a crafted CloudFormation template body containing template engine directives submitted through the product versioning API.



To remediate this issue, users should redeploy from the latest version of awslabs/virtual-engineering-workbench.

posts.content:
🚨 Synology warns of ongoing C3RB3R ransomware attacks targeting outdated NAS devices

Attackers are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to breach Synology devices running outdated DiskStation Manager versions, encrypt files and demand ransom payments.
⠀
Victims report files receiving the .L0CK3D extension alongside a read-me3.txt ransom note directing them to purchase a C3RB3R decryptor.
⠀
Synology has not identified the specific vulnerability being exploited. The linked advisory covers:

• CVE-2024-10441: Remote code execution
• CVE-2024-50629: Arbitrary file read
• CVE-2024-10445: Arbitrary file write
⠀
Users should immediately update DSM, enable automatic updates and remove the management interface from direct internet exposure.

Source: https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/synology-warns-customers-of-ongoing-c3rb3r-ransomware-attacks/

CVE-2024-10445.description: Improper certificate validation vulnerability in the update functionality in Synology BeeStation Manager (BSM) before 1.1-65374, Synology DiskStation Manager (DSM) before 6.2.4-25556-8, 7.1.1-42962-7, 7.2-64570-4, 7.2.1-69057-6 and 7.2.2-72806-1 and Synology Unified Controller (DSMUC) before 3.1.4-23079 allows remote attackers to write limited files via unspecified vectors.

posts.content: CVE-2026-120213 (CRITICAL, CVSS 9.1) impacts @fastify/http-proxy v9.0.0 – 11.6.5. Path traversal flaw lets unauthenticated attackers bypass prefix restrictions, risking SSRF. Update to 11.6.6+ ASAP. https://radar.offseq.com/threat/cve-2026-120213-cwe-22-path-traversal-in-fastifyhttp-proxy-ca54c813c9ce1f83 #OffSeq #NodeJS #infosec #CVE #vulnerability

CVE-2026-120213.description: @fastify/http-proxy is a Fastify plugin that proxies HTTP requests to an upstream server under a configured prefix. In versions 9.0.0 through 11.6.5, when an application uses parameterized prefix and rewritePrefix options to pin clients to a fixed upstream path, the plugin substitutes URL-decoded route parameters into rewritePrefix without re-encoding them. A parameter value that encodes a path separator together with a fragment or query delimiter therefore decodes into real separators and delimiters that inject extra upstream path segments and strip the mandatory suffix the rewritePrefix was meant to enforce, without using any dot-dot traversal. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use this to reach upstream locations outside the intended prefix, leading to path-restriction bypass and, depending on the upstream, server-side request forgery or authorization bypass in the proxied service. The issue is fixed in @fastify/http-proxy 11.6.6, and users should upgrade to 11.6.6 or later. There is no workaround other than upgrading.

CVE-2026-46300.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: skbuff: preserve shared-frag marker during coalescing

skb_try_coalesce() can attach paged frags from @from to @to.  If @from
has SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG set, the resulting @to skb can contain the same
externally-owned or page-cache-backed frags, but the shared-frag marker
is currently lost.

That breaks the invariant relied on by later in-place writers.  In
particular, ESP input checks skb_has_shared_frag() before deciding
whether an uncloned nonlinear skb can skip skb_cow_data().  If TCP
receive coalescing has moved shared frags into an unmarked skb, ESP can
see skb_has_shared_frag() as false and decrypt in place over page-cache
backed frags.

Propagate SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG when skb_try_coalesce() transfers paged
frags.  The tailroom copy path does not need the marker because it copies
bytes into @to's linear data rather than transferring frag descriptors.

CVE-2026-31419.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net: bonding: fix use-after-free in bond_xmit_broadcast()

bond_xmit_broadcast() reuses the original skb for the last slave
(determined by bond_is_last_slave()) and clones it for others.
Concurrent slave enslave/release can mutate the slave list during
RCU-protected iteration, changing which slave is "last" mid-loop.
This causes the original skb to be double-consumed (double-freed).

Replace the racy bond_is_last_slave() check with a simple index
comparison (i + 1 == slaves_count) against the pre-snapshot slave
count taken via READ_ONCE() before the loop.  This preserves the
zero-copy optimization for the last slave while making the "last"

posts.content:
Apache Wicket vulnerabilities: a security update fixes 19 flaws, including CVE-2026-84170 upload DoS and XSS bugs. Upgrade to 8.20.0, 9.25.0 or 10.12.0.

#ApacheWicket #Java #CVE202684170 #CVE202683594 #XSS #WebSecurity #PatchNow #Vulnerability

https://securityonline.info/apache-wicket-vulnerabilities/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-84170.description:
Allocation of resources without limits or throttling in Apache Wicket.

org.apache.wicket.markup.html.form.upload.resource.AbstractFileUploadResource is the server side of the form-less upload offered by FileUploadToResourceField, which posts the selected files to a separately mounted resource rather than through a Form. The resource is an application-wide singleton with no component to consult, so newResourceResponse() takes the three limits that bound the upload - the total request size, the maximum size of a single part and the maximum number of parts - from the request parameters maxSize, fileMaxSize and fileCountMax, and hands them to the multipart parser as they arrive. Nothing binds those numbers to the field that is supposed to be uploading. A request naming a very large maxSize is therefore parsed with no effective ceiling on the total size, and omitting fileMaxSize and fileCountMax leaves the per-part and part-count limits unset as well. The values the application configured through FileUploadToResourceField#setMaxSize(), #setFileMaxSize() and #setFileCountMax() are consulted only when the client omits the corresponding parameter, so against a client that supplies one they have no effect at all.

Parts above the parser's in-memory threshold are spooled to the container's temporary directory, and the file parts are then copied into the folder the application's IUploadsFileManager owns, under a sub-folder the request names, where they remain. A part that is not a file is read into the heap in full while the request is parsed. One request, repeatable, can therefore consume as much disk or as much heap as the client chooses to send. The resource carries no authorization annotation and the default authorization strategy permits every resource request, so unless the application authorizes the resource itself the request needs no authentication, no session, no prior page view and no user interaction.

An application is affected where it uses FileUploadToResourceField, or mounts FileUploadResourceReference itself. This is not the ordinary upload path: the resource is a singleton that has to be created and mounted deliberately. An application that configures no upload limit at all loses nothing, because Wicket applies no total-size limit of its own by default; what the defect removes is a limit the application set. Uploads through Form with FileUploadField, and through AjaxFileDropBehavior, are not affected, because both read their limits from the component rather than from the request. The upload resource does not exist in the 8.x line.

This issue affects Apache Wicket: from 9.14.0 through 9.24.0, from 10.0.0 through 10.9.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 9.25.0 or 10.12.0, which fix the issue.

posts.content:
The PostgreSQL project resolved 15 critical pgAdmin 4 vulnerabilities in version 9.19, fixing command injection flaw CVE-2026-116241 and credential leaks.

#pgAdmin4 #PostgreSQL #DatabaseSecurity #CVE2026116241 #RCE #Cybersecurity #Vulnerability #InfoSec

https://securityonline.info/pgadmin-4-vulnerabilities-fixed-9-19/?utm_source=mastodon&utm_medium=jetpack_social

CVE-2026-116241.description:
pgAdmin 4's Import/Export Data tool wraps a user's query export in a psql \copy (...) TO command and checks that the query's parentheses are balanced so that nothing can escape the wrapper. The check rejected a backslash inside a single-quoted string, but not inside a double-quoted identifier, where it treated the next double quote as closing the identifier. psql's \copy parser applies the connection's escape character to whichever quote opened a token, so with standard_conforming_strings off a backslash-escaped double quote does not close the identifier. pgAdmin's and psql's view of the quoting then diverged, a closing parenthesis hidden from the check ended the \copy (...) wrapper, and a following TO PROGRAM clause was executed by psql on the pgAdmin host, as the operating-system account running pgAdmin, before the server rejected the statement. An ordinary database role can turn standard_conforming_strings off for itself, and the Import/Export Data permission is granted to non-administrators by default.

This is a bypass of the fix for CVE-2026-17566. The fix rejects any backslash inside a double-quoted identifier, as was already done for single-quoted strings, since its meaning depends on a server setting that cannot be known reliably when the query is validated.

This issue affects pgAdmin 4: before 9.19.

CVE-2026-97638.description: The Forminator Forms – Contact Form, Payment Form & Custom Form Builder plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Insecure Direct Object Reference in all versions up to, and including, 1.57.3.1 via the 'previous_draft_id' parameter due to missing validation on a user controlled key. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary saved drafts belonging to other users and take over those draft identifiers by overwriting them with attacker-controlled form submissions. This requires the attacker to have obtained a victim's draft_id, which may be harvested from a shared "continue later" link; the nominally present nonce check is effectively bypassed because the nonce is publicly obtainable by any unauthenticated visitor loading a form page.
